column3: “An end has come” is rendered “An end!”
“Calamity one” is rendered “unique disaster”; many manuscripts read “disaster after disaster.”
“Doom” is a rare word; the meaning is uncertain. “Confusion” is rendered “tumult.”
NASB reverses the verbs: “the rod has budded, arrogance has blossomed.”
“Noise” is rendered “wealth,” and “distinction” as “anything eminent”; the Hebrew is difficult.
The second half of the verse is difficult; the meaning is uncertain.
“An impure thing” is rendered “an abhorrent thing.”
“He has made it” is rendered “they transformed.”
“Evil of nations” is rendered “worst of the nations.”
